USMLE Step 1

Universal 5-Step Master Diagnostic Frameworks & Algorithms

This document consolidates the complete, standardized diagnostic logic, decision trees, comparison matrices, and high-yield board hooks across all core systems covered in this review series.

  • 8 systems
  • 40 steps, 5 per system
  • 2 decision trees
  • 28 hot hooks

System 1 of 8 · Diagnostic framework

Endocrine System

The 5-Step Master Diagnostic Process

Step 1 to Step 5 Tap a step to open or close it

Step 1Identify the Affected Organ/Axis
Palpitations, heat intolerance, weight loss
Thyroid Axis
Hypertension, central obesity, striae, Na+/K+ shifts
Adrenal Axis
Amenorrhea, galactorrhea, bitemporal hemianopsia
Pituitary Axis
Polyuria, polydipsia, abdominal pain
Endocrine Pancreas
Kidney stones, bone pain, high/low calcium
Parathyroid / Calcium Axis
Step 2Determine Hyperfunction vs. Hypofunction

Characterize clinical state (excess secretion vs. deficiency/resistance).

Step 3Primary vs. Secondary (Upstream/Downstream Rule)
Primary (Target Gland Defect)

Trophic and Target hormones move in OPPOSITE directions (e.g., High T4 + Low TSH Primary Hyperthyroidism).

Secondary / Central (Pituitary/Hypothalamus Defect)

Trophic and Target hormones move in the SAME direction (e.g., High Cortisol + High ACTH Cushing Disease).

Step 4Dynamic Suppression & Stimulation Testing
High-dose Dexamethasone suppresses ACTH
Cushing Disease (Pituitary Adenoma).
Fails to suppress
Ectopic ACTH (Small Cell Lung CA).
Cosyntropin (ACTH) test fails to increase Cortisol
Primary Adrenal Insufficiency (Addison).
Desmopressin (dDAVP) increases urine osmolality
Central DI.
Fails to increase
Nephrogenic DI.
Step 5Pathognomonic Anchors
  • Psammoma bodies(Papillary Thyroid CA)
  • Hurthle cells(Hashimoto)
  • Painful thyroid post-viral(De Quervain)
  • Hyperpigmentation + hyperkalemia(Addison)
  • Necrolytic Migratory Erythema(Glucagonoma)

System 2 of 8 · Diagnostic framework

Renal System

The 5-Step Master Diagnostic Process

Step 1 to Step 5 Tap a step to open or close it

Step 1Broad Localization
Glomerular

Dysmorphic RBCs, RBC casts, proteinuria, hematuria, facial edema.

Tubular / Interstitial

Sterile pyuria, WBC casts, eosinophils, muddy brown casts, drug rash/fever.

Vascular

Microangiopathic hemolytic anemia + thrombocytopenia + AKI (HUS/TTP), asymmetric kidneys.

Postrenal

Flank/groin colic, hydronephrosis, suprapubic tenderness, prostatic symptoms.

Step 2Glomerular Subtyping
FeatureNephriticNephrotic
ProcessInflammatoryNon-inflammatory
Key findingsRBC casts, oliguria, HTNEdema, hyperlipidemia, fatty casts/oval fat bodies
Proteinuria<3.5 g/day>3.5 g/day
Nephritic (Inflammatory)
Low C3

PSGN (Subepithelial humps, post-strep) vs. DPGN (Lupus, wire-looping).

Normal C3

IgA Nephropathy (Synpharyngitic) vs. Goodpasture (Linear IF, hemoptysis) vs. Wegener (c-ANCA).

Nephrotic (Non-inflammatory)
Minimal Change Disease

Child, normal LM, foot process effacement on EM.

FSGS

African American, HIV, Heroin, Sickle Cell, segmental hyalinosis.

Membranous Nephropathy

Caucasian adult, Anti-PLA2R, HBV/HCV, Spike & Dome.

Step 3AKI Differentiation Matrix
IndexPrerenalIntrinsic (ATN)
BUN/Cr> 20:1< 15:1
FENa< 1%> 2%
UNa< 20 mEq/L> 40 mEq/L
UrineConcentrated Urine >500 mOsm/kgIsosthenuric Urine <350 mOsm/kg
Step 4Urinary Cast Recognition
RBC Casts
Glomerulonephritis / Nephritic
WBC Casts
Acute Interstitial Nephritis (AIN) / Pyelonephritis
Muddy Brown Granular Casts
Acute Tubular Necrosis (ATN)
Fatty Casts (Maltese Cross)
Nephrotic Syndrome
Broad Waxy Casts
End-Stage Renal Disease (ESRD)
Step 5Renal Tubular Acidosis (RTA) Fast-Track
RTA typeK+Urine pHMechanism / clue
Type 4 RTAHigh K+\u2013Hypoaldosteronism / Spironolactone / ACEi
Type 1 RTA (Distal)Low K+pH > 5.5Inability to secrete H+; stone risk
Type 2 RTA (Proximal)Low K+pH < 5.5Inability to reabsorb HCO3-; Fanconi link

System 3 of 8 · Diagnostic framework

Respiratory System

The 5-Step Master Diagnostic Process

Step 1 to Step 5 Tap a step to open or close it

Step 1Spirometry & Volume Classification
Obstructive (FEV1/FVC < 70%)

Air trapping (\u2191 TLC, \u2191 RV).

Reversible
Asthma.
Irreversible + \u2193 DLCO
Emphysema.
Irreversible + Normal DLCO + Reid Index >50%
Chronic Bronchitis.
Restrictive (FEV1/FVC \u2265 70% with TLC < 80%)
Intrinsic (\u2193 DLCO)
IPF, Sarcoidosis, Pneumoconioses.
Extrapulmonary (Normal DLCO)
ALS, Myasthenia Gravis, Scoliosis, Severe Obesity.
Step 2Hypoxemia & A-a Gradient
Normal A-a Gradient (5\u201315 mmHg)
Hypoventilation (Opioids, ALS) or High Altitude (\u2193 FiO2).
Elevated A-a Gradient + Responds to 100% O2
V/Q Mismatch (PE, COPD, Asthma).
Elevated A-a Gradient + Refractory to 100% O2
Shunt (ARDS, Atelectasis, R-to-L Cardiac Shunt).
Step 3Lung Carcinoma Localization
Central

Small Cell (Chromogranin+, ACTH/SIADH/Lambert-Eaton) & Squamous Cell (Keratin pearls, Cavitation, PTHrP Hypercalcemia).

Peripheral

Adenocarcinoma (Mucin+, non-smokers, EGFR/ALK) & Large Cell (Pleomorphic giant cells).

Step 4Pleural Effusion Light's Criteria (Exudate if ANY 1 is met)
  1. Fluid/Serum Protein > 0.5
  2. Fluid/Serum LDH > 0.6
  3. Fluid LDH > 2\u20443 upper limit of normal serum LDH
Step 5Pathognomonic Hooks
  • Curschmann spirals/Charcot-Leyden crystals(Asthma)
  • Ferruginous bodies(Asbestosis)
  • Asteroid/Schaumann bodies + Non-caseating granulomas(Sarcoidosis)
  • Steeple sign(Croup)
  • Thumbprint sign(Epiglottitis)

System 4 of 8 · Diagnostic framework

Gastrointestinal & Hepatobiliary

The 5-Step Master Diagnostic Process

Step 1 to Step 5 Tap a step to open or close it

Step 1Anatomic Localization
  • Esophageal(dysphagia/odynophagia)
  • Gastric(epigastric meal-related pain)
  • Intestinal(diarrhea/cramping/altered bowel habits)
  • Hepatobiliary(RUQ pain, jaundice, ascites)
  • Pancreatic(epigastric pain radiating to back)
Step 2Lab Profiling

Hepatocellular Pattern (AST/ALT \u226B Alk Phos): Viral, Alcoholic (AST:ALT > 2:1), NAFLD.

Cholestatic Pattern (Alk Phos \u226B AST/ALT): Choledocholithiasis, PBC (Anti-Mitochondrial Ab+), PSC (p-ANCA+, UC link), Pancreatic Head CA.

Lipase/Amylase >3\xD7 upper limit
Acute Pancreatitis.
Step 3Jaundice & Bilirubin Logic
Unconjugated (Indirect) >80%

Hemolysis vs. Impaired conjugation (Gilbert - mild, stress-induced; Crigler-Najjar - UDP-GT defect).

Conjugated (Direct) >50%

Biliary obstruction vs. Dubin-Johnson (Black liver) vs. Rotor syndrome.

Step 4Esophageal Motility vs. Mechanical Dysphagia
Dysphagia for Solids ONLY
Mechanical obstruction (Peptic stricture, Ring, Cancer).
Dysphagia for Solids AND Liquids
Motility disorder (Achalasia - loss of Auerbach plexus, bird-beak sign; Diffuse Esophageal Spasm - corkscrew; Scleroderma - low LES pressure).
Step 5Histological & Special Stain Hooks
Mallory-Denk bodies
Alcoholic Hepatitis
PAS-positive, diastase-resistant globules
\u03B11-Antitrypsin Deficiency
Prussian blue positive
Hereditary Hemochromatosis
Kayser-Fleischer rings / Low ceruloplasmin
Wilson Disease
Signet ring cells / Linitis plastica
Diffuse Gastric Adenocarcinoma
PAS-positive macrophages in lamina propria
Whipple Disease

System 5 of 8 · Diagnostic framework

Neurology & Neuroanatomy

The 5-Step Master Diagnostic Process

Step 1 to Step 5 Tap a step to open or close it

Step 1Functional Localization & Sensory Relays
  • Cortex(Aphasia, neglect)
  • Thalamus VPL(contralateral body sensory)
  • Thalamus VPM(contralateral face sensory)
  • Subthalamic Nucleus(Hemiballismus)
  • Cerebellar Vermis (Truncal ataxia) vs. Hemispheres(Limb ataxia)
Decorticate (Flexor) Posturing

Lesion ABOVE Red Nucleus. Rubrospinal intact Upper extremity FLEXION ("hands to core").

Decerebrate (Extensor) Posturing

Lesion AT/BELOW Red Nucleus (midbrain/pons). Unopposed vestibulospinal drive Upper & Lower EXTENSION (Worse prognosis).

Step 2Motor Neuron Sign Patterns
Both UMN & LMN Signs (Sensory & Autonomic SPARED)

ALS (SOD1 mutation link, death via diaphragm failure, Tx: Riluzole).

Pure LMN Signs

Werdnig-Hoffmann / SMA (SMN1 gene, floppy infant, tongue fasciculations), Poliomyelitis.

Non-Progressive Pediatric Motor

Cerebral Palsy (Periventricular leukomalacia, scissoring gait, toe walking).

Step 3Stroke & Hemorrhage Differentiation
ACA Stroke

Contralateral lower extremity motor/sensory loss.

MCA Stroke

Contralateral face/upper extremity motor/sensory loss + Aphasia.

PCA Stroke

Contralateral homonymous hemianopia with macular sparing.

Cerebral Amyloid Angiopathy (CAA)
Beta-amyloid in small cortical vessels
Recurrent lobar hemorrhages in elderly (Occipital/Parietal).
Charcot-Bouchard Microaneurysms
Chronic HTN
Deep intraparenchymal basal ganglia bleed (NOT visible on angiography).
Arteriovenous Malformation (AVM)
Direct arterial-to-venous shunt
"Bag of worms" on MRI/angiogram in young adult (10\u201340 y/o).
Step 4Trinucleotide Repeat & Genetic Matrix
Friedreich Ataxia (AR, GAA repeat, Frataxin)

Staggering gait + Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy (cause of death) + Pes cavus.

Myotonic Dystrophy Type 1 (AD, CTG repeat, DMPK)

Myotonia (cannot release handshake) + Cataracts + Frontal balding + Testicular atrophy.

Huntington Disease (AD, CAG repeat)

Caudate atrophy + Chorea + Dementia + Anticipation.

Step 5Primary CNS Tumors
Adults (Supratentorial)
  • GBM(GFAP+, pseudopalisading necrosis)
  • Meningioma(Dural tail, Psammoma bodies)
  • Schwannoma(S100+, CPA angle, Antoni A/B)
  • Oligodendroglioma(Fried-egg, chicken-wire)
Pediatric (Infratentorial)
  • Pilocytic Astrocytoma(Benign, Rosenthal fibers, GFAP+, cystic + mural nodule)
  • Medulloblastoma(Malignant, Homer-Wright rosettes, drop mets, vermis mass)
  • Ependymoma(4th ventricle, perivascular pseudorosettes)

System 6 of 8 · Diagnostic framework

Hematology & Oncology

The 5-Step Master Diagnostic Process

Step 1 to Step 5 Tap a step to open or close it

Step 1Cell Line Localization
  • Anemia/Polycythemia(RBC)
  • Mucocutaneous bleeding/petechiae(Platelets/Primary hemostasis)
  • Joint hemarthrosis/deep hematomas(Coagulation cascade/Secondary hemostasis)
  • B-symptoms/painless nodes/blasts(Leukocyte/Marrow)
Step 2Diagnostic Indices & Anemia Profiling (MCV < 80 fL)
PatternFerritinTIBCSerum Fe
Iron Deficiency AnemiaLowHigh\u2013
Anemia of Chronic Disease (Hepcidin traps iron)HighLow\u2013
Sideroblastic Anemia (Ringed sideroblasts, ALAS defect, Lead, B6 deficiency)High\u2013High
Strikingly low MCV (<70) + Normal/High RBC count
Thalassemia (\u03B2-Thal: HbA2/HbF elevated).
Step 3Primary vs. Secondary Hemostasis
Primary (ITP, TTP, HUS, vWD, Glanzmann, Bernard-Soulier)

Skin/mucosal bleeding, prolonged bleeding time, low platelets (except vWD/functional defects), normal PT/PTT.

Secondary (Hemophilia A/B/C, Vitamin K deficiency, Warfarin)

Deep joint hemarthrosis, normal bleeding time, normal platelets, prolonged PT/PTT.

Step 4Acute vs. Chronic Leukemia Differentiation
Blasts \u2265 20% (Acute)

ALL (Child, TdT+, CD10/CALLA+, t(12;21) good) vs. AML (Adult, MPO+, Auer Rods, t(15;17) APL subtype with high DIC risk, treated with ATRA).

Blasts < 20% (Chronic)

CLL (Elderly, CD5+ B-cell, Smudge cells, AIHA risk) vs. CML (Granulocytes, t(9;22) BCR-ABL1, low LAP score, Tx: Imatinib).

Step 5High-Yield Chromosomal Translocations
t(15;17)
Acute Promyelocytic Leukemia (APL / M3; RAR-\u03B1 fusion, Auer rods, DIC risk).
t(9;22)
CML (Philadelphia chromosome; BCR-ABL1 constitutive tyrosine kinase).
t(8;14)
Burkitt Lymphoma (c-MYC overexpression, starry-sky histology, EBV link).
t(14;18)
Follicular Lymphoma (BCL-2 overexpression, anti-apoptotic).
t(11;14)
Mantle Cell Lymphoma (Cyclin D1 overexpression, G1/S transition).

System 7 of 8 · Diagnostic framework

Reproductive & Breast Pathology

The 5-Step Master Diagnostic Process

Step 1 to Step 5 Tap a step to open or close it

Step 1Anatomic & Tissue Localization

Uterus: Dysmenorrhea + enlarged globular uterus ( Adenomyosis) vs. asymmetric enlarged uterus ( Fibroids).

  • Breast: Mobile mass in young female( Fibroadenoma)
  • bloody nipple discharge without mass( Intraductal Papilloma)
  • leaf-like stroma( Phyllodes)
  • "Indian file" single row cells( Invasive Lobular CA)
Step 2Infective Vaginitis & STI Ulcer Differentiations
Vaginitis
Thin, gray + fishy odor + pH > 4.5
Bacterial Vaginosis (Clue cells).
Frothy yellow-green + strawberry cervix + pH > 4.5
Trichomoniasis (Motile flagellates).
Cottage cheese + intense pruritus + normal pH (<4.5)
Candida (Pseudohyphae).
Genital Ulcers
Painless
Syphilis (Chancre), LGV (C. trachomatis L1\u2013L3; suppurative buboes), Granuloma Inguinale (Donovan bodies).
Painful
Genital Herpes (Grouped vesicles, HSV-2), Chancroid (H. ducreyi; school of fish).
Step 3Disorders of Sex Development (DSD) Fast-Track
46,XY + NO UTERUS
High Testosterone
Androgen Insensitivity Syndrome (Female phenotype, blind vagina).
Low Testosterone
5\u03B1-Reductase Deficiency (Ambiguous until virilization at puberty).
45,XO + UTERUS PRESENT
Ovarian Dysgenesis / Streak Ovaries
Turner Syndrome (Coarctation, bicuspid aortic valve, shield chest).
46,XX + UTERUS PRESENT
High 17-OH Progesterone
Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia (21-OH deficiency; virilization).
Normal 17-OHP
M\xFCllerian Agenesis (Blind vagina, ovaries normal).
Step 4Ovarian Tumor Biomarkers & Histology
Serous Cystadenocarcinoma
CA-125, Psammoma bodies.
Dysgerminoma
hCG/LDH, "Fried-egg" cytoplasm.
Yolk Sac (Endodermal Sinus)
AFP+, Schiller-Duval bodies (glomeruloid).
Granulosa Cell Tumor
Estrogen/Inhibin+, Call-Exner bodies (eosinophilic fluid follicles).
Fibroma
Meigs Syndrome (Fibroma + Ascites + Right hydrothorax).
Step 5Gestational Trophoblastic Disease

Complete Mole: 46,XX/XY (empty egg + 2 sperms), NO fetal tissue, markedly high \u03B2-hCG, snowstorm ultrasound.

Partial Mole: 69,XXX/XXY (1 egg + 2 sperms), PARTIAL fetal tissue present.

System 8 of 8 · Diagnostic framework

Musculoskeletal & Rheumatology

The 5-Step Master Diagnostic Process

Step 1 to Step 5 Tap a step to open or close it

Step 1Peripheral Nerve Entrapment & Lesion Rules
Median Nerve
Proximal (Supracondylar fracture)
Hand of benediction on fist making.
Distal (Carpal tunnel)
Median claw at rest.
Recurrent Branch (Superficial palm cut)
Pure Motor thenar OAF loss, NO sensory loss.
Radial Nerve
Main trunk (Mid-shaft humerus)
Wrist drop + dorsal sensory loss.
PIN / Deep branch (Supinator)
Pure Motor finger drop (NO wrist drop, NO sensory loss).
Superficial branch (Handcuffs)
Pure Sensory loss over dorsal hand.
Ulnar Nerve
Proximal (Elbow)
Milder clawing (Ulnar paradox) + dorsal/palmar sensory loss.
Distal (Guyon canal)
Severe Ulnar claw + palmar sensory loss ONLY.
Deep branch (Palm)
Pure Motor intrinsic hand loss.
Step 2Inflammatory vs. Non-Inflammatory Joint Disease
FeatureOsteoarthritis (OA)Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA)
ProcessDegenerative wear-and-tearAutoimmune pannus
With useworsens with useimproves with use
Morning stiffness<30 min>1 hr
Jointsasymmetric, DIP involved (Heberden nodes)symmetric PIP/MCP (SPARES DIP)
Hallmarksosteophytes/eburnationAnti-CCP (most specific), RF (anti-IgG Fc)
Step 3Inflammatory Myopathies Comparison
Polymyositis

Endomysial inflammation, CD8+ T cells, symmetric proximal weakness, Anti-Jo-1.

Dermatomyositis

Perimysial inflammation, CD4+ T cells, symmetric proximal weakness, Gottron papules, Heliotrope rash, Shawl sign, associated with underlying internal malignancy.

Inclusion Body Myositis

Elderly males, asymmetric distal weakness (wrist flexors), rimmed vacuoles with \u03B2-amyloid.

Step 4Crystal Arthropathy Fast-Track
FeatureGoutPseudogout (CPPD)
CrystalMonosodium urateCalcium pyrophosphate
Shapeneedle-shapedrhomboid-shaped
Birefringencestrongly NEGATIVELY Birefringentweakly POSITIVELY Birefringent
Colour under polarized lightYellow when parallel to polarized lightBlue when parallel
Clinical cluePodagra (1st MTP joint), triggered by alcohol/loopsChondrocalcinosis on X-ray, Knee most common
Step 5Collagen & Hereditary Disorders
Osteogenesis Imperfecta

Type I Collagen mutation (COL1A1/COL1A2), brittle bones, multiple fractures, blue sclerae, hearing loss.

Ehlers-Danlos

Type V (Classic) or Type III (Vascular) Collagen mutation, hyperextensible skin, hypermobile joints, tissue fragility/vascular rupture.

Marfan Syndrome

Autosomal dominant FBN1 mutation (Fibrillin-1), tall stature, arachnodactyly, lens subluxation UPWARD, aortic root aneurysm/dissection.

Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy
X-linked recessive frameshift mutation in Dystrophin
complete loss of dystrophin, Gowers sign, calf pseudohypertrophy, elevated CK.

Summary · All systems

Universal Pathognomonic "Hot Hooks" Summary

28 hooks

  • Psammoma BodiesPapillary Thyroid Carcinoma, Meningioma, Serous Cystadenocarcinoma of Ovary, Mesothelioma.
  • Orphan Annie Eye NucleiPapillary Thyroid Carcinoma.
  • Hurthle CellsHashimoto Thyroiditis.
  • Subepithelial Humps on EMPoststreptococcal Glomerulonephritis (PSGN).
  • Linear ImmunofluorescenceGoodpasture Syndrome (Anti-GBM).
  • Apple-Green Birefringence under Polarized Light (Congo Red)Amyloidosis.
  • Ferruginous BodiesAsbestosis (golden-brown dumbbell fibers).
  • Charcot-Leyden Crystals & Curschmann SpiralsAsthma.
  • Mallory-Denk BodiesAlcoholic Hepatitis.
  • PAS-Positive, Diastase-Resistant Globules\u03B11-Antitrypsin Deficiency.
  • Kayser-Fleischer RingsWilson Disease (Low ceruloplasmin).
  • Rosenthal FibersPilocytic Astrocytoma.
  • Homer-Wright RosettesMedulloblastoma / Neuroblastoma.
  • Auer RodsAcute Myelogenous Leukemia (AML) / Acute Promyelocytic Leukemia (APL).
  • Reed-Sternberg Cells (CD15+, CD30+)Hodgkin Lymphoma ("Owl-eye" nuclei).
  • Smudge CellsChronic Lymphocytic Leukemia (CLL).
  • Teardrop Cells (Dacrocytes) + Dry TapPrimary Myelofibrosis.
  • Schistocytes / Helmet CellsMicroangiopathic Hemolytic Anemia (MAHA: TTP, HUS, DIC).
  • Heinz Bodies & Bite CellsG6PD Deficiency.
  • Call-Exner BodiesGranulosa Cell Tumor of Ovary.
  • Schiller-Duval BodiesYolk Sac / Endodermal Sinus Tumor (AFP+).
  • Reinke CrystalsLeydig Cell Tumor.
  • KoilocytesHPV 16/18 infection (Cervical Dysplasia / CIN).
  • Clue CellsBacterial Vaginosis (Gardnerella).
  • Donovan BodiesGranuloma Inguinale (Klebsiella granulomatis).
  • Gottron Papules & Heliotrope RashDermatomyositis.
  • Codman Triangle & Sunburst PatternOsteosarcoma.
  • Onion-Skin Periosteal Reaction + t(11;22)Ewing Sarcoma.
